- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) — cap forecast growth after 2-3 consecutive days of high sentiment or price surge.
- Forecast horizon 30d often shows lag: true price moves 1-2 days ahead of model; shift forecast 1-2 days forward to match actual momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to “stick” to prior trend; introduce smoothing or momentum decay factor to avoid overfitting.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction for next 5-7 days to prevent over-optimism.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) or low (0.33) for 3+ days, model often underperforms; increase forecast baseline by 1-2% to account for low volatility bias.
